valuation_chain.actual_valuation: Valuation R (WithZero Multiplicative Int), with legendreBound defined by the three actual integer logarithms; no supplied valuation laws.
exhaustive_cases: v(lambda)>1: v(lambda-1)=v(lambda) and numerator polynomial valuation=v(lambda)^2
valuation_chain.case_proof: Direct valuation unequal-term sum/subtraction identities, ultrametric inequality, and polynomial identities. Cases lemma omits the nonzero/not-one assumptions and remains valid at lambda=0 and lambda=1.
valuation_chain.log_j: Uses exact 256*(lambda^2-lambda+1)^3/(lambda^2*(lambda-1)^2); denominator nonzero follows from lambda != 0 and lambda != 1. NeZero 2 makes 256 nonzero.
valuation_chain.upper: v(256)<=1 gives log v(256)<=0; all four cases prove max(0,log v(j))<=legendreBound. Valuation-j-zero branch is explicit.
valuation_chain.lower: v(256)=1 and valuation j != 0 retain the exact source lower result. Applies only to odd residue characteristic at the finite-place step.
valuation_chain.field_generality: Pure algebraic lemmas require only the stated Field/valuation and where needed NeZero 2; no curve/provider/Tate/theta parameter introduced.

finite_normalization.actual_invariants: residueChar is the existing ring characteristic of the actual residue field; inertDeg and ramIdx are Mathlib Ideal.inertiaDeg / ramificationIdx at the actual maximal ideal; localDeg=e*f; completionAt is the actual adic completion.
finite_normalization.normalization: Under-prime equality identifies (p); norm of maximal ideal is p^f. Actual finite-place real log is integer valuation log multiplied by f*log p. Pointwise finWeight is f*log p, not e*f*log p.
finite_normalization.positive_weight: p is prime hence p>1; f>0; finWeight>0 is proved from actual Mathlib invariants.
finite_normalization.posLog_conversion: log+ value = finWeight * max(0, integer valuation log), with nonzero input hypothesis before the logarithmic conversion.
finite_normalization.all_primes_upper: 256 is an actual algebraic integer, so its valuation<=1 at every finite place, including residue characteristic 2.
finite_normalization.odd_prime_lower: 2 belongs to the maximal ideal iff residue characteristic=2; outside 2 its actual valuation equals1, hence valuation256=1. No characteristic-2 lower claim is made.

support_and_counting.finite_support: For nonzero y uses actual FinitePlace.hasFiniteMulSupport and support inclusion; y=0 is handled separately with empty support.
support_and_counting.common_support: suppFinset is the union of supports of all four actual functions: log+lambda, log+lambda inverse, log+(lambda-1) inverse, log+j. Proven support inclusion turns original all-place finsums into exact finite sums.
support_and_counting.compact_triple: The actual K membership bounds absolute logs of generator and generator-1. Positive-log and inverse-log lemmas supply all three needed finite bounds at every place over V.
support_and_counting.count_chain: For q prime, actual ideals below each place lie over (q); injectivity of place->maximal ideal and subset of all primes over q permit sum(e*f)<=finrank. For q nonprime, filter is empty because every actual residue characteristic is prime.
support_and_counting.inertia_and_cardinality: e>=1 gives sum f<=sum e*f; f>=1 gives number of places over each q<=sum f. Finite union over arbitrary V yields card(filter(S,residueChar in V))<=V.card*deg x.
support_and_counting.lower_sum: Splits same common support into over-V and outside-V. Over-V contribution <=6*c times count; outside-V odd-prime pointwise lower bound applies using 2 in V. Remainder j terms are bounded by full j sum using nonnegativity. Exact final error 6*c*V.card*deg x retained.

special_cases.lambda_zero_or_one: Actual parents are on existing Pt, which excludes both; gen_ne_zero/gen_ne_one supply needed denominators. Pure exhaustive cases itself still covers these boundary values.
special_cases.j_zero: Upper theorem explicitly simplifies j=0 to zero positive logarithm. Lower theorem retains j != 0; existing final composer continues to use the separate sixth-root argument when j=0.
special_cases.empty_or_negative_bound_K: No global c>=0 is assumed. Lower proof derives c>=0 only from an actual member hx via existing c_nonneg, so empty K.set remains valid.
special_cases.q_zero_one_or_composite: Counting proof handles all q via nonprime-empty-filter branch; no false log-positive fact is used there.
